name: Abacha (African Salad)
summary: Shredded dried cassava tossed in a creamy palm oil and potash sauce with ugba, garden egg leaves, fish and crunchy onion.
story: Abacha is an Igbo dish of dried, shredded cassava that is soaked and tossed with a palm oil sauce, ugba and toppings. It is often served as a snack or starter at gatherings, topped with fish, ponmo or garden eggs.

items.name: Potash (kaun)
items.note: mixed with 3 tbsp water, see swaps

steps.title: Soak the abacha
steps.text: Place the abacha in a bowl and cover with hot water. Leave for about 3 minutes, then drain and rinse. Cover with cold water and soak for 30 to 60 minutes until the strands are tender but still have a slight bite.

steps.title: Rinse the ugba
steps.text: Rinse the ugba in warm water for a minute to remove excess smell, drain well and set aside.

steps.title: Make the potash liquid
steps.text: Dissolve the potash in 3 tbsp of water. Leave to settle and pour off the clear liquid, leaving any sediment behind.

steps.title: Thicken the palm oil
steps.text: In a large bowl or pot, combine the palm oil with 1 tbsp of the clear potash liquid. Stir over very low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until it turns thick, creamy and a lighter yellow-orange.

steps.title: Season the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the crayfish, ehuru, pepper, cube, chopped onion and salt. Taste: it should be well seasoned.

steps.title: Fold in the abacha and ugba
steps.text: Drain the abacha well. Add it with the ugba to the sauce and toss gently until every strand is coloured. Add fish and half the utazi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile onto plates and garnish with the sliced onion, remaining utazi and sliced garden egg. Serve at room temperature.

tips: Do not oversoak the abacha or it turns slimy. Test a strand for texture.
Add potash liquid gradually. Too much tastes harsh.
Drain the abacha thoroughly or the sauce will turn watery.
Add toppings at the end to keep them crisp.

swaps.swap: Thin rice noodles briefly soaked are a distant stand-in for texture only. The flavour will differ.
Leave it out, or use finely sliced steamed green beans for texture.
A pinch of baking soda in water; use sparingly.
